item.content:encoded:
Hollandia Yoghurt is showcasing the different ways consumers can enjoy the product as part of everyday meals and snacks through its “Yoghurt It How You Want It” campaign, while reaffirming its commitment to delivering quality products to Nigerian consumers.

The campaign highlights how Hollandia Yoghurt can be enjoyed beyond a standalone beverage, featuring in breakfast options, snacks, smoothies and simple recipes. This consumer-focused approach is underpinned by Hollandia’s commitment to quality, with products carrying the masterbrand made with careful consideration and best-in-class quality processes.


Speaking on the campaign, Olugbenga Akindele, Category Head, Dairy, said the initiative combines the brand’s focus on quality with an invitation for consumers to explore different ways to enjoy Hollandia Yoghurt.

“At Hollandia, quality remains central to our commitment to consumers. Our products are made with careful consideration and best-in-class quality processes, reflecting our commitment to delivering products consumers can enjoy with confidence. Through our ‘Yoghurt It How You Want It’ campaign, we want consumers to discover more ways to enjoy Hollandia Yoghurt, whether as part of breakfast, a quick snack or their favourite food combinations,” he said.

Hollandia Yoghurt can be paired with popular snacks such as meat pies, sausage rolls and puff-puff, or combined with fruits and granola to create breakfast bowls and parfaits. It can also be blended with fruits to prepare smoothies or incorporated into selected recipes.


The range offers consumers different flavour options to suit their preferences. Hollandia Strawberry brings a fruity taste to breakfast bowls and smoothies, while Hollandia Vanilla offers a creamy flavour for combinations such as pancakes, granola and parfaits. Hollandia Plain Sweetened provides another option for pairing with fruits, nuts and other toppings.

Available in 315ml and 1L packs, Hollandia Yoghurt caters to different consumption occasions, from individual refreshment to household use and food preparation.

Through the “Yoghurt It How You Want It” campaign, Hollandia is encouraging consumers to explore different ways to incorporate Hollandia Yoghurt into their routines, with product quality remaining central to the brand’s commitment to Nigerian households.

item.title: Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Nigerian-born Shirley U. Emehelu has been sworn in as New Jersey's Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State, becoming the state's first immigrant to hold the office and joining its first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team.

The post Nigerian-Born Shirley Emehelu Makes History as New Jersey’s First Immigrant Lieutenant Governor appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Shirley U. Emehelu, New Jersey’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Photo Credit: Official Site of New Jersey

A Nigerian-born legal leader has made history in New Jersey. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill has officially appointed Nigerian-American Shirley U. Emehelu as the state’s fifth Lieutenant Governor and Secretary of State. Sworn in at the New Jersey Statehouse in Trenton on 9 November 2026, Emehelu has made double history in the process—becoming New Jersey’s first immigrant Lieutenant Governor and forming part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team.

Born in Nigeria before moving to the United States at the age of three, Emehelu brings an extraordinary record of public service and legal excellence to New Jersey’s second-highest executive office. Before this historic appointment, she served as Acting State Comptroller, leading key efforts to combat fraud, waste, and abuse while protecting taxpayer funds and strengthening government accountability, and also stepped in as Acting Secretary of State to oversee New Jersey’s elections.

Her public sector résumé also includes a two-year tenure as Executive Assistant Attorney General of New Jersey, where she served as the third-ranking official in the New Jersey Attorney General’s Office. In that role, she directly counselled the Attorney General, coordinated oversight for more than 500 attorneys within the Division of Law—New Jersey’s largest legal office—and directed civil defence and enforcement matters across civil rights, environmental protection, labour and consumer protections, data privacy, and firearms safety.

New Jersey Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu, part of the state’s first all-women Governor–Lieutenant Governor team. Photo Credit: Shirley U. Emehelu/LinkedIn

Earlier in her career, Emehelu spent nine years at the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of New Jersey, serving as Chief of Asset Recovery and Anti-Money Laundering, where she prosecuted complex financial fraud cases and oversaw statewide asset forfeiture and victim restitution programmes. She also practised in the private sector as a member of the White-Collar Criminal Defense and Government Investigations Group at CSG Law, co-leading the firm’s Banking and Finance Group, after clerking for the Honourable James R.Spencer in the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Virginia.

An alumna of Yale University (where she earned her B.A.) and Yale Law School (where she earned her J.D.), Emehelu is a proud resident of Montclair, New Jersey, where she and her husband, Ike, raised their two children, Nnamdi and Amara.

Speaking on the appointment, Governor Mikie Sherrill praised Emehelu’s track record in accountability and public service, noting:

From prosecuting financial fraud and rooting out waste and abuse, to defending civil rights and protecting consumers, Shirley has fought for New Jersey families at every step of her career. Shirley also maintains strong leadership at the Secretary of State’s office after successfully overseeing the smooth administration of our elections last week. She pairs the highest ethical standards with the same tenacity to run toward our toughest challenges, and I am proud to have her by my side as we work to deliver for the people of New Jersey.

Accepting the historic appointment, Lieutenant Governor Shirley U. Emehelu shared:

I am honoured by Governor Sherrill’s trust and the opportunity to serve the people of New Jersey as Lieutenant Governor. I’ve spent my career upholding the law, protecting families, and rooting out fraud, abuse, and corruption. As Lieutenant Governor and continuing my role as Secretary of State, I’ll bring that same tenacity to lowering costs, expanding opportunity for every community, and ensuring government delivers for the people we serve.

item.content:encoded:
The Forum for Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) successfully concluded its 2026 annual convention on Thursday, October 29, at the historic Glover Memorial Hall in Lagos, Nigeria. Convening under the theme “One Industry, Many Voices: Building Together,” the afternoon brought together over 200 practitioners from several sectors including; film, television, radio, advertising, and digital media to connect, share insights, and build mutual agency.

Supported by the African Women’s Development Fund (AWDF), the convention featured a keynote address by cultural curator Sandra Mbanefo Obiago, interactive panel sessions, break-out workshops, speed networking, and a flagship fireside chat titled “The Cross Over: A Career Beyond Borders.”

The event drew leading voices from across the creative economy, including media executive Kadaria Ahmed, filmmaker Biodun Stephens, media personality Gbemi Olateru-Olagbegi, executive director Rosemary Egabor-Afolahan, and director Esosa Osagiede.

Key takeaways and actionable resolutions from the convention sessions emphasized resilience, strategic partnerships, and structural evolution: Embrace Bold Collaboration and Risk-Taking: Speakers urged media professionals to shed apprehension around institutional partnerships. As highlighted during the panel discussions:

“Do not allow fear of failing stop you from asking for help, do your due diligence on the people you want to partner with then go for it. If it does not work, do not stop, get up and go again.”

Adaptability as a Survival Imperative: In an era of rapid technological and digital shifts across broadcast and film, participants were reminded of the absolute necessity of evolution: “If you don’t change with the times, you will grow stale.” Deconstructing Industry Myths: Addressing professional dynamics, panelists challenged antiquated narratives regarding female competition, affirming that systemic progress relies on solidarity: “Women work well with women, it is a myth that they do not.”

FWIFT’s leadership noted that the conversations at Glover Memorial Hall mark a critical step toward cementing cross-sector alliances. The forum remains committed to translating these insights into actionable frameworks, mentorship programs, and policy advocacy for women shaping the future of African media.

For more information on upcoming FWIFT initiatives, programs, and future events, visit the official website or follow @fwiftnigeria on social media.

About FWIFT Nigeria

The Forum For Women in Film and Television Nigeria (FWIFT) is a professional organization dedicated to empowering Nigerian women in screen-based, audio, and digital media through advocacy, skill acquisition, mentorship, and strategic networking.

item.content:encoded:
Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels.

There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience.

However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives.

I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies.

The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles.

During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within.

However, there was a challenge.

Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief.

Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation.

Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. This created unnecessary friction, and I found myself having to mediate whenever issues arose, even though the service I had been engaged to provide was recruitment.

I eventually had a lengthy conversation with one of the founders, explaining that communicating reporting lines and responsibilities during recruitment was only one part of the process. The organisation also needed to formally implement the new structure, clarify authority and ensure that everyone understood and respected the changes.

Unfortunately, the founders believed they could figure things out themselves. Eventually, I had to distance myself from the recurring back-and-forth. Looking back, this experience reflects some of the mistakes many start-up founders make when trying to build and manage their businesses.

Here are five of them:

Recruitment is not all a business needs

Understandably, start-up founders want to manage expenses, especially when the business is still trying to establish itself. However, trying to save money on essential business processes can eventually become more expensive.

Some founders believe they can figure everything out themselves or that hiring the right people is all they need to get the business running smoothly. Unfortunately, recruitment is only one part of building an effective organisation.

Beyond hiring, businesses need proper onboarding processes, clearly defined roles and responsibilities, HR policies, performance management systems and standard operating procedures (SOPs).

Investing in the right professional services from the beginning can help prevent avoidable challenges and create a solid foundation for business growth.

Allowing personal relationships to influence business decisions

There is nothing wrong with employing relatives, friends or people personally known to the founders. However, personal relationships should not take precedence over professional responsibilities and organisational policies.

For instance, a founder might appoint a relative or close associate to oversee a department without properly defining their responsibilities, qualifications, reporting lines or accountability.

What happens when that person begins to exercise authority beyond their designated role? What happens when other employees are expected to report to someone whose position and responsibilities have not been properly communicated?

These situations can create unnecessary tension, undermine management authority and make it difficult to hold people accountable. Every employee, regardless of their relationship with the founder, should understand their role, work within established reporting structures and be held to the same professional standards.

Organisational structure is not only on paper

Having an organisational chart, clearly defined job descriptions or stating reporting lines in employees’ offer letters is not enough to ensure that a business runs smoothly. These structures must be properly implemented and communicated across the organisation.

For instance, hiring a new manager and communicating to every newly recruited employee that they are expected to report to this person. However, the existing employees are still accustomed to reporting to someone else who previously occupied a position of authority. If management does not formally communicate the changes, transfer the necessary authority and ensure that everyone understands the new arrangement, conflicts are likely to arise.

This is why restructuring goes beyond recruiting new employees or assigning responsibilities. It requires management to communicate the changes, establish clear reporting lines, delegate authority and ensure that everyone understands and respects the new structure.

Who makes decisions? Who supervises each department? Who approves expenses? Who handles employee grievances? Who is responsible for ensuring that company policies are implemented?

These are important questions that every founder should be able to answer and ensure that the appropriate people within the organisation understand. Without proper implementation, even the most carefully designed organisational structure may exist only on paper, leaving employees confused, managers struggling to exercise authority and founders constantly having to resolve avoidable operational issues.

Making the founder the centre of every business decision

If you are the person making every decision in your business, approving every request, resolving every employee disagreement and overseeing every little detail, you may have built a business that depends entirely on your presence rather than one that can operate effectively without you.

Think about it. Can you leave your business for two whole weeks without constantly worrying that everything will fall apart in your absence?

If the answer is no, then it may be time to reconsider how your business is structured.

Effective delegation is not simply about assigning tasks to employees. It involves putting the right people in leadership positions, establishing clear processes and giving employees the authority and resources they need to carry out their responsibilities.

When these systems are properly implemented, the founder can focus on business development, strategic partnerships, expansion and other important decisions instead of being involved in every operational activity.

Failing to invest in employee development and performance management

Hiring experienced employees does not mean they no longer need training or professional development. Every organisation has its own processes, expectations and standards. Employees need to understand these requirements and receive periodic training to ensure they can perform their responsibilities effectively.

Founders should also establish a performance management system that allows employees to receive regular feedback, understand their performance expectations and identify areas where improvement is necessary.

This could involve quarterly performance appraisals, one-on-one check-ins, skills-gap assessments and learning and development programmes. When employee development is treated as an ongoing process, businesses are better positioned to improve productivity, retain good employees and build internal capacity.

item.content:encoded:
“Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. 

Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. 

I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. 

You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life.

I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day.

There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. 

Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. 

I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. 

But this experience is not unique to me.

Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. 

The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate.

On the village aspect, families now live further apart than ever before thanks to japa, and even those within Nigeria struggle to come together for various reasons, one of which is high transportation costs. 

While there are certainly challenges, becoming a mother at an older age can also have its advantages.

You tend to be more mature, grounded in your identity, and confident in your choices. You have a clear understanding of the kind of child or children you wish to raise and are intentional in selecting a partner who aligns well with your values. Additionally, because you have prioritised building wealth, you have more resources at your disposal, which can significantly enhance the comfort of both you and your child. This financial stability helps you avoid being in survival mode, allowing you to approach motherhood with greater calmness. Research shows that well-regulated mothers often raise emotionally balanced children. You also have the means to hire highly qualified staff from reputable nanny agencies to assist in caring for your child.

One potential advantage—or disadvantage, depending on your perspective—of becoming pregnant at age 35 or older is the increased likelihood of having twins. As women approach menopause, natural biological changes in hormone levels can raise the chances of conceiving non-identical (fraternal or dizygotic) twins. This could be exciting if you have a preference for twins, but it may be something to consider carefully if you do not.

There are several ways to ensure that age doesn’t truncate your dreams of motherhood. The most important one is taking care of your mind and your body.  Exercise, eat a balanced diet, and prioritise protein and fibre. Schedule yearly check-ins with your OB-GYN to check your overall health, among other things.

Take your vitamins seriously, especially folic acid. Try to avoid added sugar as much as you can. Get at least 8 hours of sleep every day. Most importantly, do not give in to the fear-mongering online. Women age 35 and above can and do get pregnant without any medical interventions, going on to have healthy babies. And even if you end up needing medical intervention, it is nothing to be ashamed of.

Finally, while you wait to start your own family, go out, have fun, travel the world if you can afford to, and live your life to the fullest. Trust me, I know what it’s like.

Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade (Toni Tones), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives.

Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms, Seun Ajayi, Fae Olumide, Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba.

Created and directed by Wande Thomas (Under the Influence, The Smart Money Woman), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi (The Smart Money Woman, Ci) .

Director and creator Wande Thomas added:

I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it.

F Taofeeq/Spiraling

Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said:

With Spiraling, we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora.

Ladun Awobokun, Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented :

Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. We’re delighted to bring it to our viewers.

Spiraling will be available to stream on KAVA on the 26th of November. Follow @spiralingseries for updates.

Damson Idris stars as Prince Inan in the official trailer for Paramount Pictures’ Children of Blood and Bone.

A fantasy world rooted in African mythology, a star-studded cast and Lagos as one of its filming locations: Children of Blood and Bone is bringing a major African story to the big screen. Paramount Pictures has unveiled a new trailer for the film adaptation of Tomi Adeyemi’s bestselling fantasy novel, giving us a glimpse of Thuso Mbedu, Tosin Cole, Amandla Stenberg and Damson Idris in the fantasy adventure.

Directed by Gina Prince-Bythewood, who co-wrote the screenplay alongside Adeyemi, the film brings the fantastical kingdom of Orïsha to life. The story centres on Zélie Adebola, a young divîner who sets out on a high-stakes quest to restore magic to her oppressed people. Alongside her brother Tzain, Zélie forms an unlikely alliance with Princess Amari and Prince Inan, the daughter and son of the ruthless King Saran, as they fight back against his tyrannical rule.

From left: Lashana Lynch, Tosin Cole, director Gina Prince-Bythewood, Amandla Stenberg, Thuso Mbedu, Cynthia Erivo, Chiwetel Ejiofor, and Damson Idris at New York Comic Con. Photo Credit: Children of Blood and Bone/Instagram 

Filmed on location in Lagos, Nigeria, the production brings together an impressive global and homegrown cast. Thuso Mbedu leads the film as Zélie, starring opposite Damson Idris as Prince Inan, Amandla Stenberg as Princess Amari and Tosin Cole as Tzain. The cast also features screen legends Viola Davis as Mama Agba, Idris Elba as Lekan, Chiwetel Ejiofor as King Saran, Regina King as Queen Nehanda, Cynthia Erivo as Admiral Kaea and Lashana Lynch as Jumoke.

Celebrating Nigerian talent, the film also stars Nollywood icon Richard Mofe–Damijo, Zackary Momoh as Adetayo, Grammy-nominated singer Ayra Starr, Bukky Bakray, Temi Fagbenle, Shamz Garuba, Kola Bodunde and Pamilerin Afolake Ayodeji.

Adding to the cultural excitement, the new trailer offers a preview of “African Love Story“, a brand-new original track by Grammy-winning Nigerian singer Tems, who serves as executive music producer and curator for the official Children of Blood and Bone soundtrack. Making history as the first woman to executive produce a film soundtrack on this scale, Tems contributes three original songs to the project, with Burna Boy joining as executive music consultant.

Co-stars Amandla Stenberg, Thuso Mbedu, and Cynthia Erivo pose together during the Children of Blood and Bone press tour at New York Comic Con. Photo Credit: Thuso Mbedu/Instagram 

The soundtrack lineup brings together an exciting range of African and international music talent, including Burna Boy, Ayra Starr, Fireboy DML, BNXN, Obongjayar, Show Dem Camp, Moelogo, Pa Salieu, Daecolm, Kold AF and Moonchild Sanelly. The project also features an original film score composed by Terence Blanchard.

Children of Blood and Bone arrives in cinemas and IMAX on 15 January 2027, with wider UK, Nigerian and international cinema releases beginning on 22 January 2027.

item.content:encoded:
Nigerian DJ and philanthropist Florence Otedola, popularly known as Cuppy, pictured wearing gold headphones and a camel-brown blazer.

On her birthday, Florence Ifeoluwa Otedola is giving viewers a more personal glimpse into her life, exploring home, family, identity and purpose.

For years, Nigerians have known Florence “Cuppy” Otedola as the internationally recognised DJ and philanthropist, often recognised by her signature pink hair and vibrant public personality. This birthday, however, her new documentary offers a closer look at the woman behind that familiar public image.

Released on 11 November 2026, her new 12-minute documentary, Ifeoluwa, follows Cuppy back to Lagos, the city that shaped her and remains close to her heart. It is also a place connected to some of her greatest successes and deepest heartbreak.

The title Ifeoluwa means “The Love of God”. Rather than marking the occasion with another glamorous birthday celebration, Cuppy has chosen to share a more reflective portrait of her life. The film explores womanhood, ambition, identity, belonging and the ongoing process of becoming.

There are tender moments, too. Viewers see Cuppy not just as a public figure, but as a daughter, sister and granddaughter. Her time with her grandmother offers an especially intimate glimpse into the affection and family ties at the heart of her story.

The documentary also captures an evolution audiences may already have noticed. Her signature pink hair has given way to a new look, while faith, education and service have become increasingly central to how Cuppy speaks about her future. This is not a rejection of music, but a fuller picture of the person behind it.

Her philanthropic work remains an important part of that picture. Through the Cuppy Foundation, she has helped raise more than $17 million to support displaced children in Nigeria, in partnership with Save the Children. She has also established education funds at the University of Oxford, New York University and King’s College London to help students overcome financial barriers, particularly those from Africa.

Alongside this work, Cuppy remains active as an international DJ, with performances at Glastonbury, Wireless Festival and Cannes Lions, as well as events during United Nations General Assembly week.

At its heart, Ifeoluwa is a personal homecoming that brings together family, faith, Lagos and the experiences shaping Cuppy’s next chapter. It offers viewers a chance to see beyond the familiar celebrity image and learn more about the person behind it.

item.content:encoded:
With NTDA leading the national delegation, NTT Global Destinations mobilising international partnerships and diaspora networks, and NANTA representing Nigeria’s private tourism sector, the Nigeria Pavilion became a vibrant celebration of culture, community and tourism opportunities.

For three exciting days, Nigeria brought its rhythm, culture, hospitality and entrepreneurial spirit to the global stage at World Travel Market (WTM) London 2026, held from 3 to 5 November at ExCeL London.

Led by the Nigerian Tourism Development Authority (NTDA), under its Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, the Nigeria Pavilion welcomed international visitors, tourism professionals, Nigerians and Africans living in the United Kingdom, and industry stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria.

Supporting the national showcase was NTT Global Destinations (NGD), NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, responsible for coordinating the exhibition’s planning, stakeholder engagement, international liaison and delivery.
Together with the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA) and diaspora media partners, Nigeria created an experience that extended beyond destination marketing.

Day One: Nigeria Arrives in Colour and Rhythm

The opening day brought the Nigeria Pavilion to life with traditional talking drums, cultural performances, networking and opportunities for visitors to experience Nigeria’s creative identity.

From the energetic rhythms to conversations about Nigeria’s tourism offering, the pavilion quickly became a gathering point for visitors interested in discovering more about the country.

Among the highlights was the opportunity to connect Nigerian culture with the global appeal of Nollywood, Afrobeats and contemporary African creativity.

The Director General Who Stole the Show

Perhaps one of the most memorable moments came when NTDA Director General, Dr Olayiwola Awakan, joined the traditional drummers and dancers in an energetic cultural performance.

Rather than remaining a spectator, the DG became part of the attraction, embracing the rhythm and excitement of the Nigerian showcase.

His performance drew attention and captured the spirit of the exhibition: a country confidently presenting its culture to the world.

It was tourism diplomacy in its most authentic form, demonstrating that sometimes the most powerful way to promote a destination is simply to experience and celebrate it.

Day Two: Tourism, Tradition and Private Sector Connections

The second day combined cultural discovery with industry engagement, featuring a traditional palm wine experience, networking and interactions between Nigerian tourism stakeholders and international visitors.

An important part of Nigeria’s participation was the presence of the National Association of Nigeria Travel Agencies (NANTA), one of the foremost voices of Nigeria’s organised travel trade.

NANTA’s participation celebrated the longstanding contribution of Nigerian travel professionals to the country’s international tourism visibility.

Its members brought industry experience, entrepreneurial energy and professional networks, reinforcing the importance of private sector participation in international tourism promotion.

Together, NTDA, NGD and NANTA demonstrated the value of collaboration between government institutions, strategic implementation partners and tourism businesses.

The Power of the Diaspora: Bringing the Community to Nigeria

One of the defining features of the Nigeria Pavilion was the remarkable turnout of Nigerians and other Africans living in the United Kingdom, alongside tourism stakeholders who travelled from Nigeria.
Throughout the exhibition, the pavilion became a lively meeting point where culture, community and tourism conversations came together.

This strong diaspora presence also reflected the international relationships cultivated by Elizabeth Agboola, Founder and CEO of NTT Global Destinations.

Through its established networks and collaboration with DJA Media, a diaspora media and community engagement partner, NGD helped connect Nigeria’s official tourism showcase with Nigerian and African communities across the United Kingdom.
These relationships contributed to the atmosphere, visibility and community participation that distinguished the pavilion.

For NGD, the experience reinforced an important principle: the African diaspora is not simply an audience for tourism promotion. It is an influential network for destination advocacy, cultural diplomacy, trade connections and market access.
The turnout illustrated how community relationships can strengthen national participation at international exhibitions, creating opportunities that extend beyond formal meetings and institutional representation.

Day Three: Nigerian Day and a Celebration of National Identity

The final day brought together the cultural energy and connections that had defined the exhibition, culminating in the Nigerian Day celebrations.

With music, cultural expression and national pride at the centre of the experience, the pavilion closed its three day showcase on a celebratory note.

Beyond the performances, the exhibition highlighted Nigeria’s tourism potential, its creative industries and the opportunities for greater international collaboration.

Beyond the Exhibition: NGD’s Vision for Tourism Diplomacy and Market Access

While the cultural performances attracted attention, an equally important story unfolded behind the scenes.
As NTDA’s Strategic and Pavilion Implementation Partner, NTT Global Destinations supported Nigeria’s participation through exhibition coordination, international stakeholder engagement, pavilion delivery and the mobilisation of industry and diaspora networks.

Led by Elizabeth Agboola, NGD continues to position itself at the intersection of tourism development, international market access, Africa and diaspora engagement, and tourism diplomacy.

The company’s approach recognises that successful international destination promotion requires more than exhibition space. It requires institutional relationships, private sector participation, community networks and sustained international engagement.
Nigeria’s WTM London 2026 participation provided a practical demonstration of how these elements can work together.

For NGD, the broader ambition is to help transform tourism visibility into meaningful opportunities for trade, investment, destination development and international cooperation.

One Pavilion, One Shared Nigerian Story

Nigeria’s presence at WTM London 2026 was ultimately a celebration of collaboration.
From NTDA’s institutional leadership and the memorable cultural participation of its Director General, to NANTA’s private sector representation, NGD’s strategic coordination and the enthusiastic support of the diaspora, the pavilion showcased the collective strength of Nigeria’s tourism community.

The drums brought the rhythm. The diaspora brought the energy. The tourism professionals brought the industry expertise.
And together, they brought Nigeria’s story to life on the global stage.


NTT Global Destinations is a tourism development and international market access company working across tourism, Africa and diaspora engagement, and the Halal economy. The company supports destination promotion, strategic partnerships, tourism diplomacy and international market development.

item.content:encoded:
The 12th edition of Africa’s biggest cocktail celebration, Lagos Cocktail Week (LCW), brought its 2026 theme, “Africa Pours into Lagos,” to life in spectacular fashion, delivering an exciting fusion of Pan-African creativity, cross-border collaborations, spirited competitions, and immersive experiences that celebrated the continent’s vibrant and evolving cocktail culture.

Held from October 16 to 23, 2026, the week-long festival took cocktail culture beyond borders, bringing together some of the most exciting talents and bar communities from Lagos, Accra, and Abidjan. At the heart of this year’s celebration was a powerful message: Africa’s cocktail industry thrives when creativity, culture, and expertise flow freely across borders.

The celebrations took off on Sunday, October 18, as the Italian Trade Agency brought a touch of Italian sophistication to the festival with the Italian Cocktail Experience, an exclusive, invitation-only masterclass and Aperitivo Italiano held at Mr Panther, Victoria Island. The experience offered guests an opportunity to explore the artistry and traditions of Italian cocktail culture. Speaking at the event, Maurizio Ferri, Director of the Italian Trade Agency, highlighted the initiative’s goal of promoting Italian wines and spirits, featuring brands such as Campari, Aperol and Martini.

The experience began with a masterclass hosted by Lara Rawa, founder of Lagos Cocktail Week, exploring five Italian classics: the Negroni, Americano, Bellini, Aperol Spritz and Garibaldi. Guests learned about the Italian aperitif tradition and how individual palates shape cocktail preferences.

The evening continued with networking, Italian wine and cocktail tastings, and special guests, including Chef Gibbs and visiting bartenders from Abidjan and Ghana. With music by DJ Exclusive, the event combined cultural exchange, education and entertainment in celebration of Italian cocktail culture.

One of the most exciting additions to this year’s festival was the debut of the Lagos Bar Show, a fresh take on the traditional bar hop that brought the spirit of Pan-African collaboration directly into some of Lagos’ most exciting bars.

On Tuesday, October 20, Sora Lagos played host to the first guest shift, welcoming the team from Bissa, Abidjan, for an exciting collaboration featuring Dodo Plantain Infused Rum.

The following evening, Wednesday, October 21, the spotlight shifted to Praia Lagos, where bartenders from Accra’s Front/Back and No. 19 Bar & Restaurant brought a taste of Ghana’s cocktail scene to Lagos, with Audry Cognac taking centre stage. The guest bartenders took over the bar, creating a selection of signature cocktails with Audry Cognac as their base. Front/Back’s bartenders served the Mantse and Ashanti, while the team from No. 19 Bar & Restaurant presented the Akwaaba, meaning “welcome,” and Nkabom, meaning “togetherness.”

Praia Lagos’ bartenders also showcased their creativity with Audry Cognac, serving the Audry Passion Sour and Audry Old Fashioned. The evening drew professional bartenders, mixologists and cocktail enthusiasts, who gathered to support the guest teams and celebrate the culture of bartending and mixology.

The lively event combined Ghanaian cocktail influences with Lagos’ vibrant bar scene, creating memorable moments of cultural exchange, collaboration and celebration.

Beyond the cocktails and celebrations, Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 also reinforced its commitment to industry growth, knowledge-sharing, and professional development. On Thursday, October 22, the festival’s industry conference took place at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Lagos, bringing together bartenders, hospitality entrepreneurs, brand representatives, and key industry stakeholders for conversations about the future of Africa’s cocktail and hospitality landscape.

The conference explored the theme “Shaping the Future of Hospitality”. It brought together hospitality professionals and industry stakeholders to explore opportunities and emerging trends across Nigeria’s beverage and hospitality sectors.

Discussions covered the business behind the bar, the future of beverage service at Nigerian events, gastro mixology, wine pairings, modern cocktail techniques and the future of mixology in Nigeria. Speakers included Jeremiah George, founder of Liquids by Zen; Emem Udom, founder of Apotheca Mixology; Folakemi Alli-Balogun, founder of The Wine Club Lagos; Benedicta Ogar, CEO of Cavodah and founder of SAHA Africa; Olawuyi Babatunde Abinibi, creative director of Abinibi Events Cottage; and Captain Gibbs, chef and founder of the Nigerian Food Summit.

The conference provided a platform for knowledge-sharing, industry collaboration and conversations on advancing hospitality standards and shaping the future of Nigeria’s cocktail and beverage industry.

The excitement reached its peak on October 22 and 23 with the highly anticipated Cocktail Village, transforming the Balmoral Convention Centre at the Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, into a vibrant playground of cocktails, music, entertainment, and unforgettable experiences.

Across two exhilarating days, cocktail enthusiasts were treated to unlimited cocktails, immersive brand activations, live performances, and opportunities to discover exciting new flavours, interact with their favourite brands, and connect with fellow lovers of cocktail culture.

Adding a competitive edge to the festivities was the crowd-favourite Bar Battle, which saw talented mixologists put their creativity, technical skills, and showmanship to the test in a thrilling contest for the coveted title of Lagos Cocktail Week Champion across three brand-sponsored challenges.

In the Absolut Challenge, Onaghise Kingsley Osagie won ₦1 million, while Samuel Olubunmi Ayodele received ₦500,000. The MONIN Challenge saw Valentine Justin take first place with ₦500,000, followed by Benjamin Terna (₦300,000) and Aghama Gabriel (₦200,000).

In the Johnnie Walker Challenge, Victoria Chiamaka emerged as Lagos Cocktail Champion, winning ₦1 million, while Aghama Gabriel and Victor Ceasar received ₦200,000 and ₦100,000, respectively, for their innovative serves. Other finalists received ₦200,000 voucher cards redeemable at Legend Supermarket.

The competition celebrated the creativity and talent driving Nigeria’s growing mixology industry.

The festival came to a spectacular close on Friday, October 23, with the Cocktail Village Grand Finale, bringing together an exciting mix of partner activations, entertainment, and celebratory moments. Adding to the night’s electric atmosphere was an energetic performance by dynamic duo Wanni X Handi, providing a fitting finale to eight days of cocktail-inspired experiences.

While the curtains have closed on Lagos Cocktail Week 2026, the impact of this year’s edition extends far beyond the festivities. Through its celebration of African talent, cross-border collaborations, and commitment to industry development, the festival continues to strengthen its position as a leading platform for cocktail culture, creativity, and hospitality innovation across the continent.

Lagos Cocktail Week 2026 was proudly supported by Absolut, Casamigos Tequila, Johnnie Walker, Gordon’s, Tanqueray, Lord’s Gin, Natterjack Irish Whiskey, Smirnoff X1, Gold Bar Whiskey, Schweppes, Nestlé Pure Life, West Cork Distillers, Orijin, MONIN, Cutty Sark, Bolt, Eventi Cocktails, Sip Pass, Ocean5 Riviera and Balmoral.

item.content:encoded:
Olamide releases his new single Burukutu alongside his upcoming album Time & Space. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram

If Olamide‘s ‘Burukutu‘ has been on repeat, here’s something else to get into: the rapper has revealed the cover art and full tracklist for his upcoming album, Time & Space.

Scheduled for release on November 16, 2026, under YBNL Nation and EMPIRE, the ten-track body of work follows a remarkable lineage of musical evolution from one of Africa’s most enduring creative forces. Adding a deeply personal touch to the rollout, Olamide revealed that he personally painted the striking cover art for the project.

Olamide hand-painted the official artwork for his upcoming Time & Space, released via YBNL Nation and EMPIRE. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram

Listeners have already caught an exciting glimpse of what to expect from the record through the release of the lead single, Burukutu. Named after the traditional, locally brewed fermented grain beverage, the track serves up rich street-level jubilation and celebratory culture, anchored by rhythmic cadences and unmistakable Yoruba-inflected delivery. The musical journey of Time & Space spans ten carefully curated titles designed to showcase his artistic range.

The newly revealed tracklist opens with “Elohim” as the introductory piece, followed sequentially by “Skoskola“, “Say Less“, the lead anthem “Burukutu“, and “Alujon” rounding out the first half. The second half picks up the tempo with “Mbiri“, the collaborative track “Jaiye” featuring vocalist Fola, followed by “Oshey“, “Ring“, and the closing record “Jogor“. Keeping features remarkably streamlined, the album highlights a targeted guest appearance from Nigerian singer Fola, allowing Olamide’s distinctive penmanship and vocal direction to take centre stage across the entire tracklist.

The official 10-track tracklist for Olamide’s album Time & Space, featuring lead single Burukutu and a guest appearance by Fola. Photo Credit: Olamide/Instagram

This forthcoming release arrives as the direct successor to his self-titled studio album, Olamidé, which dropped in June 2025 with a sprawling 17-track setup featuring heavyweights like Wizkid. Where that previous body of work leaned into massive collaborative constellations, Time & Space scales back into a more intimate, focused exploration of sound, anchored tightly by the creative vision of the YBNL boss himself. As November 16 approaches, anticipation continues to build across Lagos and beyond, cementing yet another brilliant chapter in Olamide’s legendary catalogue.

item.content:encoded:
Achraf Hakimi with his trophy after winning African Player of the Year at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: CAF/Instagram

For the first time in 12 years, Lagos will host the CAF Awards, with the 2026 ceremony scheduled for Wednesday, 2 December. The event, which was originally set for 7 December, will bring together leading African footballers, coaches and teams at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts in Iganmu.

Spanning 18 award categories across men’s and women’s football, the 2026 CAF Awards will celebrate the finest players, coaches, national teams, and clubs across the continent while bringing football royalty, Nollywood stars, Afrobeats performers, and fashion insiders together on one red carpet.

The 2026 shortlists come with a notable twist for the host nation. No Nigerian player made the ten-man shortlist for the CAF Men’s Player of the Year award—leaving out Super Eagles stars Victor Osimhen and Ademola Lookman alongside Egypt’s Mohamed Salah—and no Nigerian footballer features in the CAF Women’s Player of the Year category either, with three-time Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year winner Chiamaka Nnadozie also absent from the final lists.

Chiamaka Nnadozie celebrating her third consecutive Goalkeeper of the Year win at the 2025 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: Chiamaka Nnadozie/Instagram

Even so, Nigeria still has four nominations to look forward to on home soil on 2 December. The Super Falcons are nominated for Women’s National Team of the Year alongside Algeria, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, Ghana, Malawi, Mali, Morocco, and South Africa. In the individual women’s categories, Edo Queens and Falconets shot-stopper Christiana Uzoma represents Nigeria on the Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year shortlist, while Nigerian youth internationals Seimeyeha Janet Akekoromowei and Oluwakemi Adegbuyi are both in the running for Women’s Young Player of the Year.

Elsewhere, the headline races feature some of the biggest names in global football. Defending winner Achraf Hakimi of Morocco and Paris Saint-Germain leads the CAF Men’s Player of the Year nominees alongside his compatriots Brahim Diaz and Ismael Saibari, Senegal’s Sadio Mané, Ismaila Sarr, and Pape Gueye, Côte d’Ivoire’s Amad Diallo, Ghana’s Antoine Semenyo, DR Congo’s Yoane Wissa, and South Africa’s Teboho Mokoena.

Ademola Lookman celebrating his Men’s Player of the Year victory at the 2024 CAF Awards. Photo Credit: Ademola Lookman/Instagram

Over in the CAF Women’s Player of the Year race, Zambia’s Barbra Banda and Malawi’s Tabitha and Temwa Chawinga headline a competitive ten-player shortlist that also includes South Africa’s Thembi Kgatlana, Ghana’s Portia Boakye, Algeria’s Marine Dafeur, Morocco’s Hanan Ait El Haj, and Cameroon trio Marie Ngah Manga, Michaely Bihina, and Monique Ngock. Other major honours on the night include Men’s and Women’s Goalkeeper of the Year, Interclub Player of the Year, Coach of the Year, Young Player of the Year, National Team of the Year, and Club of the Year.

With voting running from 5 November to 20 November 2026, all roads lead to the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts in Lagos on Wednesday, 2 December, where African football’s biggest names will gather for a night of sport, music, and celebration.

item.content:encoded:
Maltina has unveiled its refreshed visual identity at a trade launch event in Lagos, marking 50 years of nourishing Nigerian homes and introducing a new look for the iconic malt brand while retaining the taste and nutritional qualities consumers have come to love.

Held on Friday, November 6, 2026, at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Ikeja, the event brought together business partners, distributors, consumers and other distinguished guests to celebrate the milestone and experience the refreshed brand through interactive activities, entertainment and product showcases.

First introduced as Maltona in 1976 and renamed Maltina in 1977, the brand has maintained a strong presence in Nigerian homes for over five decades. Its journey has been defined by a commitment to nourishment, including its introduction of multivitamin enrichment in 1993 and calcium fortification in 2009. Beyond its product innovations, Maltina continues to build meaningful connections with consumers through initiatives such as Maltina Nourishment Tour, Maltina Dance All, Maltina Teacher of the Year (MTOTY), and its Christmas and Ramadan festive campaigns, creating opportunities for learning, participation and shared experiences.

Speaking at the event, Sarah Agha, Marketing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., reflected on the brand’s journey and the thinking behind its refreshed identity. She highlighted Maltina’s longstanding commitment to nourishment and happiness, noting that the new look represents a more contemporary and confident expression of the brand as it prepares for its next chapter.

The refreshed packaging features an enriched signature orange, gold accents and barley elements that reinforce Maltina’s malt credentials. The updated sunrays represent vitality and optimism, while the more prominent calcium coin highlights its nourishment proposition. The gold crown cork and the addition of ‘Since 1976’ further celebrate the brand’s heritage.

She reassured consumers that while the brand’s visual identity has evolved, its familiar taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged.

She said “This is not just about refreshing our identity; it is about reaffirming our commitment to nourishment and to families across Nigeria. Our new look makes these commitments even more visible. While our identity has evolved to welcome a new chapter, our taste and nutritional credentials remain unchanged. It is still New Look, Same Nourishing Taste,” 

In his welcome address, Thibaut Boidin, Managing Director, Nigerian Breweries Plc., celebrated Maltina’s remarkable journey and acknowledged the consumers, partners and distributors whose continued support has contributed to the brand’s growth. He also reiterated the company’s commitment to social impact, announcing plans to support the education of children from underserved communities in the coming year.

The unveiling was brought to life through a creative performance by Hermes Iyele, combining poetry, dance and music around the theme of rebirth, followed by a celebratory toast led by Nigerian Breweries executives.

Elohor Olumide-Awe, Portfolio Manager, Non-Alcoholic Brands, Nigerian Breweries Plc., and Daniella Ogunsanya, Senior Brand Manager, Maltina, shared perspectives on the brand’s refreshed identity and its next chapter.

Elohor introduced the Whats Your Word campaign, which invites consumers to engage with Maltina’s new look by expressing their impressions of the refreshed identity in ONE word. The campaign forms part of the brand’s broader consumer engagement activities designed to bring the new Maltina experience closer to Nigerians.

The event also featured a series of interactive games, including Nourishment Darts, Maltina Dance Hall and B-Quick, where guests tested their skills, explored Maltina’s nutritional benefits and competed for exciting prizes.

The top three participants, Peace, Modesinuola and Alexa, received gifts, while the overall winner received an exclusive five-day, all-expenses-paid stay at Eko Hotel. The evening ended on a high note with energetic musical performances by Wande Coal and DJ Brightstar, who kept guests entertained with popular hits and lively mixes. 

Consumers can also join the What’s Your Word campaign by visiting maltina.nbplc.com and submitting ONE word that describes the brand’s refreshed identity.

As Maltina celebrates 50 years in Nigeria, its refreshed identity signals the beginning of another chapter for the brand, building on a legacy of nourishment and happiness while retaining the taste generations of consumers have come to love.

item.title: How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look
item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.description:
Alex Unusual reimagines Yoruba traditional fashion in a fuchsia satin buba, emerald-green and magenta damask mini skirt, and matching gele at the Loving Itohan premiere.

The post How to Style a Pink Buba With a Mini Skirt: Alex Unusual’s Loving Itohan Look appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today!.
item.content:encoded:
Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses.

Who says a buba has to be paired with a wrapper? Nigerian actress, media personality, and reality television star Asogwa Alexandra A—popularly known as Alex Unusual—is giving us another way to wear the traditional Yoruba top, and her look for the premiere of Loving Itohan makes a strong case for pairing it with a mini skirt.

The actress chose a bright fuchsia satin buba with wide half-sleeves, styling it with a fitted mini skirt made from emerald-green and magenta floral brocade damask. It’s an interesting way to rethink the familiar iro and bubacombination: keep the traditional top, swap the wrapper for a shorter skirt, and let the difference in fabric and colour give the outfit its character.

The smooth finish of the pink satin against the patterned damask also shows how to wear two statement fabrics without making them compete. The trick is to give each piece a clear role, with the pink buba providing a bold block of colour and the brocade bringing in pattern and texture.

Alex Unusual puts a modern spin on the Yoruba iro and buba with a satin top and brocade mini skirt.

The mini skirt also gives the outfit a contemporary take on the Oleku silhouette, which traditionally pairs a loose or fitted buba with a wrapper tied above the knee. Alex’s version plays with that familiar proportion, using a fitted damask skirt in place of the wrapper. If you are wondering how to wear a buba and mini skirt without the proportions feeling off, the secret is balancing volume with structure. Because a traditional buba comes with a relaxed cut and wide sleeves, tucking it cleanly into a fitted, high-waisted mini skirt defines the waist and keeps the silhouette neat rather than boxy. Mixing textures intentionally helps too—pairing a plain silk, satin, or AsoOke top with a patterned damask, jacquard, or beaded mini skirt lets both pieces complement each other rather than clash.

Alex Unusual in her contemporary Yoruba buba and mini skirt outfit for the Loving Itohan premiere.

She carried the damask into her gele, which was wrapped high into voluminous, sculptural folds. An oversized gold lip-shaped brooch secured one side, adding another detail to the headpiece. Using the same fabric for the skirt and gele also helped bring the different parts of the outfit together, while keeping the pink buba at the centre of the colour story. It’s a styling idea worth borrowing if you’re working with patterned damask and want your accessories to feel connected to the rest of your outfit.

Alex Unusual pairs her damask gele with cherub-detailed sunglasses, layered gold jewellery, and custom grillz.

Alex’s jewellery and accessories added even more detail. She layered a crystal floral choker with a long gold lariat necklace featuring a stirrup-style drop, then added chunky gold cuff bangles on both wrists and sculptural gold rings. Custom gold grillz gave the traditional-inspired outfit a more personal touch, while narrow, rectangular gold-rimmed sunglasses with miniature cherubs along the top bar introduced a retro detail. She finished with a metallic gold crescent-shaped clutch and hot-pink ankle-strap platform heels, the latter picking up the colour of her buba.

Alex Unusual’s gold grillz, crystal floral choker, and cherub-accented sunglasses.

For anyone styling a pink buba, Alex’s choice of accessories offers another useful idea: bring in a second colour from the outfit through your shoes or bag, then use metallic jewellery to tie everything together. She kept her beauty look relatively understated, with defined brows, soft neutral eyeshadow, a hint of emerald liner, and glossy nude lips. Long, neutral-toned nails completed the look.

lex Unusual shows off the back tailoring of her fuchsia buba, damask mini skirt, and sculptural gele.

Alex Unusual in a pink satin buba, brocade damask mini skirt, and matching gele for the Loving Itohan premiere.

item.content:encoded:
Olumide Oworu has declared his candidacy for the Federal House of Representatives to represent Surulere Constituency 1 in 2027. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram

Actor and media personality Olumide Oworu has declared his intention to contest for the Federal House of Representatives seat for Surulere Constituency 1 in the 2027 general elections. He will be running under the platform of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM).

Olumide, who grew up in Surulere, Lagos, has a long-standing connection to the constituency. He began his acting career as a child, appearing in television productions such as Everyday People, before gaining wider recognition for his role in The Johnsons and other Nigerian film and television projects.

This is his second attempt to enter legislative politics. In 2023, he declared his intention to contest for a seat in the Lagos State House of Assembly under the Labour Party. However, administrative challenges prevented his name from appearing on the final ballot.

Olumide Oworu’s official campaign poster for the House of Representatives seat representing Surulere Constituency 1 under the Allied Peoples Movement. Photo Credit: Olumide Oworu/Instagram

Reflecting on that experience in his candidacy announcement on Instagram, Olumide said the support he received from young people in Surulere had strengthened his belief in their readiness for more active participation in governance.

“Despite the administrative hurdles that left our names off the final ballot, your resilience showed me that our vision was never a passing phase. Instead, it was the beginning of something much more significant,” he wrote.

Explaining his decision to contest again, this time for a seat in the House of Representatives, he added: “We cannot afford to sit on the sidelines while our future is decided by a political class that won’t have to live with the consequences of today’s choices.”

His campaign has highlighted issues including gaps in public services, community infrastructure and the participation of young Nigerians in policy decisions. Announcing his candidacy, he said he looked forward to continued support as he and his supporters worked towards what he described as a mission to “Reset Nigeria”.

item.title: Awar Odhiang Named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026

item.description:
Awar Odhiang has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026. The 25-year-old South Sudanese-Canadian model accepts the honour at London's Royal Albert Hall on 30 November, following her historic Chanel finale and eight international covers this year.

item.content:encoded:
Awar Odhiang featured in Vogue wearing a floral printed dress and sculpted oversized rose headpiece. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

Remember the model who turned the finale of Matthieu Blazy‘s first Chanel show into one of the most talked-about runway moments of 2025? That was Awar Odhiang, and she has another major reason to celebrate. The South Sudanese-Canadian model has been named Model of the Year at The Fashion Awards 2026.

The 25-year-old will receive the honour at London’s Royal Albert Hall on 30 November. Born in a refugee camp in Ethiopia and raised in Canada, Awar’s journey to the international fashion scene has taken her from being discovered in Alberta to walking some of the world’s biggest runways. She is now represented by major modelling agencies across London, Milan, Paris and New York.

Awar Odhiang walking the red carpet at the 2026 Met Gala in New York City. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

Her runway résumé includes shows for Prada, Versace, Miu Miu, Saint Laurent and Jacquemus, but it was her appearance at Chanel’s Spring/Summer 2026 show in October 2025 that introduced her to an even wider audience. Closing Matthieu Blazy’s first collection for the fashion house, Awar wore the show’s bridal look, featuring an oversized white shirt and a voluminous, colourful feathered skirt. But it was what happened at the finale that captured everyone’s attention.

As the models gathered for their final walk, Awar broke formation, smiling, clapping and twirling in her skirt. When Blazy appeared, she ran towards him and embraced him. The spontaneous moment quickly went viral, with fashion fans celebrating the joy she brought to the runway. It was also a historic appearance: Awar became only the third Black woman to close a Chanel show in the house’s 115-year history, after Alek Wek and Adut Akech.

Model of the Year 2026 winner Awar Odhiang backstage at the Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

Since then, her career has continued to gather pace. Awar has appeared on eight international magazine covers this year and fronted campaigns for Chanel, Chloé, Louis Vuitton, Saint Laurent, Loro Piana and H&M. She has also used her growing platform to speak up for greater representation and inclusion of Black models in the luxury fashion industry.

Awar Odhiang in Daniel Roseberry’s Schiaparelli Spring 2026 Haute Couture collection in Paris. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

Her Model of the Year recognition celebrates a remarkable year of runway, editorial and campaign work, as well as the influence she continues to have beyond the catwalk. On 30 November, she’ll take that recognition to the Royal Albert Hall, adding another milestone to a career that is still unfolding.

Awar Odhiang wearing a tailored blazer during international fashion week. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

Awar Odhiang attending the 2026 Met Gala in custom Chanel by Matthieu Blazy. Photo Credit: Awar Odhiang/Instagram

item.content:encoded:
The Francophone African Music Industries Fair (SIMA) announces the third edition of the event, taking place on November 12–13, 2026, in Cotonou, Republic of Benin.

Following its previous edition, which brought together more than 6,700 participants and over 3,000 industry professionals, this pan-African gathering dedicated to the cultural and creative industries returns with a clear ambition: African Music: From the Stage to Global Influence.

 SIMA 2026 is supported by major institutional and private-sector partners, including the Ministry of Culture, Arts and Heritage of Benin,the Ministry of Tourism and Foreign Trade of Benin,the Embassy of France in Côte d’Ivoire,the BOAD Foundation, as well as SACEM, Sony Music and Warner Music Africa. These partnerships reflect the growing interest in the
development and structuring of Africa’s cultural and creative industries.

For the second consecutive year, Benin will host SIMA, in line with the country’s broader efforts to strengthen the role of the cultural and creative industries in the structural transformation of its economy and to enhance its cultural influence at both regional and international levels.

Co-founded in 2022 by cultural entrepreneur Mamby Diomandé and artist and producer Pit
Baccardi, SIMA has established itself as a platform dedicated to structuring, connecting and
developing Africa’s creative ecosystems.

By placing music at the heart of a broader reflection on the transformation of culture and the creative industries, SIMA also seeks to address the technological shifts reshaping the sector—from artificial intelligence to new ways of creating, distributing and consuming content.

At a time when Africa’s creative economy could generate up to 20 million jobs by 2030, the
2026 edition aims to take a further step forward by contributing to the positioning of African
creativity as a powerful driver of soft power, value creation and international influence.

“African music is no longer simply a cultural phenomenon: it has become a force of influence. Our challenge now is to transform this influence into sustainable economic power. SIMA aims to build connections between creators, investors, institutions and markets so that the international visibility of our talents translates into measurable data, content monetization, economic opportunities, jobs and value creation for the continent.” Mamby Diomandé, Co-Founder of SIMA

Three Priorities for Turning Creativity into Economic Power

To address the challenges of a rapidly evolving global market, SIMA 2026 will structure its programme around three key priorities.

The first focuses on competitiveness and internationalization, with the aim of strengthening the economic performance of industry stakeholders and facilitating the international export of African talent.

The second emphasizes cross-sector collaboration, bringing music closer to fashion, film, tourism, sports and other creative industries in order to unlock new revenue opportunities.

The third focuses on public policy, intellectual property and regulatory frameworks, with the
ambition of developing concrete recommendations and strengthening the mechanisms that will enable the sector to better capture the value it generates.

Beyond discussions and professional exchanges, SIMA aims to make creativity a genuine driver
of connection across the ecosystem. Through its artist residency, live sessions and immersive
formats, the event encourages collaboration between artists, producers, industry professionals and international stakeholders, while creating bridges between African markets and the
international creative economy.

A Week at the Crossroads of Creativity, Business and Influence

From November 7–11, 2026, SIMA Lab. Music will bring together artists and beatmakers from across the continent for an artistic residency designed to produce a collaborative EP, with distribution by an international major label under consideration.

On November 12–13, 2026, the professional days and panels will bring together key players from the music ecosystem to explore major issues shaping the future of the industry, including
artificial intelligence, copyright, mobility, financing and emerging market opportunities.

At the intersection of the cultural and sports industries, a dedicated session will also explore
the convergence between football and music, two powerful drivers of influence across the continent, with the participation of sports executives and opinion leaders.

As part of this dynamic, Makaya, SIMA’s showcase platform dedicated to discovering new talent, will spotlight emerging artists from Togo, Kenya, Madagascar and other African countries, providing a new stage for the next generation of talent.

The programme will also feature the presentation of the Hamed Bakayoko Award, an honorary distinction recognizing the commitment of a patron to the development of Africa’s cultural and creative industries.

On November 14, 2026, SIMA will extend the experience through a tourism circuit organized
in collaboration with Benin Tourism, inviting artists, professionals and international guests to
discover the heritage and iconic sites of Benin. This immersive experience will give participants an opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of the host country’s cultural, historical and tourism assets, while extending networking and exchanges beyond the professional framework of the event.

About SIMA

Created and initiated by music industry experts, the Francophone African Music Industries
Fair (SIMA) promotes the African music industry, provides training and capacity-building
opportunities for ecosystem stakeholders, and facilitates business connections between
African and international industry players. As a true platform for connecting the cultural and
creative industries, SIMA provides ecosystem stakeholders with a space to create, learn,
share, connect and foster new collaborations, while contributing to discussions on the
cultural, economic and technological issues shaping Africa’s creative industries and their
international reach.

For more information Visit the official SIMA website https://www.simaonline.net

The Beninese-born singer, who rose to prominence as one of Afrobeats’ leading voices after joining Mavin Records, is set to perform on both weekends of the festival, Sunday, April 11, and Sunday, April 18, 2027. Coachella will take place at the Empire Polo Club in Indio, California.

It’s been a big year for Ayra, with her third studio album, Starrgirl, adding to an already exciting run. Fans heading to the festival can look forward to hearing songs from the project, including “Tornado” and “Midnight in New York“, as well as her collaboration “Gimme Dat“. There’s also room for crowd favourites such as “Rush“, “Commas” and “Heaven Baby“.

Ayra shares the Sunday bill with headliner SZA, alongside Victoria Monét, Jorja Smith, Becky G and Don Toliver. The wider festival, running from April 9 to 11 and April 16 to 18, will also feature headliners Dua Lipa and Tame Impala, with Madonna set for a special appearance in the dance tent.

Her Coachella booking follows another major moment in London, where she performed at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of the NFL International Games halftime show, becoming the first African artist to headline the show.

And there’s even more for fans to look forward to. Ayra has announced her 20-city Starrgirl World Tour, which will take her across Europe and North America in early 2027 before she heads to the California desert for Coachella. What a year ahead for the Starr girl.
